Two Seeds
TOO SEEDZ
noun
From Genesis 3:15, the enmity between the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent; the two spiritual lineages of Scripture.

📖 Biblical Definition

The two seeds are the two spiritual lineages set in enmity by the first promise of the gospel: I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed. From the curse upon the serpent runs the whole history of redemption as a conflict between the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent—between the line of faith and the line of the world, the children of God and the children of the devil—until the woman’s Seed should bruise the serpent’s head, though His own heel be bruised. Cain and Abel, Isaac and Ishmael, Jacob and Esau trace the parting of the two ways through the generations; the godly line is preserved and the enmity persists. The apostle Paul shows that the promised Seed is ultimately one—to Abraham and his seed were the promises made; he saith not, And to seeds, as of many, but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. In Christ the head of the serpent is crushed: the Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil. The Lord Himself told the unbelieving that they were of their father the devil. The dictionary reads the two seeds as the spiritual antithesis running through all Scripture and history, resolved at the cross where the woman’s Seed, the Lord Jesus, bruised the serpent’s head and secured His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

From Genesis 3:15; the two spiritual lineages—the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent—in enmity through history until Christ, the woman’s Seed, bruised the serpent’s head.

TWO SEEDS, the enmity of Genesis 3:15 between the woman’s seed and the serpent’s.

The conflict of the line of faith and the line of the world through history.

Traced in Cain and Abel, Isaac and Ishmael, Jacob and Esau.

The promised Seed is ultimately one, which is Christ (Gal 3:16).

Christ was manifested to destroy the works of the devil.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 3:15 — "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."

Gal 3:16 — "Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ."

1Jo 3:8 — "He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil."

Joh 8:44 — "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The biblical two seeds are corrupted by the “serpent-seed” heresy, which makes the seed of the serpent a literal carnal lineage and breeds racial and dualist error; the seeds of Scripture are spiritual, parted by faith and unbelief.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption to name is the “serpent-seed” heresy, which twists the two seeds of Genesis 3:15 into a literal, carnal genealogy—teaching that Eve had relations with the serpent and bore Cain, so that a physical line of the devil’s offspring walks the earth. This fable has fed racial hatred and a dualism foreign to Scripture, and it has appeared among the Two-Seed-in-the-Spirit Predestinarian sects and in fringe teachers. The Bible knows no such carnal devil-seed. The enmity of the two seeds is spiritual: the children of God and the children of the devil are distinguished by faith and unbelief, by the new birth and its absence, not by bloodline.

The principle to recover is the spiritual antithesis resolved in Christ. The seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are the line of faith and the line of unbelief, running through every nation and family; men become children of God by the new birth and children of the devil by abiding in sin. And the great Seed is one—Christ, in whom the promise is fulfilled and the serpent’s head crushed. He was manifested to destroy the works of the devil, and all who are His by faith share His victory over the ancient enemy.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Genesis 3:15; the spiritual enmity of the woman’s seed and the serpent’s, resolved in Christ, who bruised the serpent’s head.
